Article Title: Woman dies after ChatGPT convinces her to change her medication dosage; Google CEO Sundar Pichai had flagged this risk with AI models three years ago
Article Text:
Google CEO Sundar Pichai

What Sundar Pichai said in 2023

Previous death cases associated with ChatGPT

A lawsuit against OpenAI has highlighted the risks of relying on artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots for health advice. Qun Wan and Meiqin Xu filed a lawsuit October 27, 2026, over the death of their 31-year-old daughter, Bowen Wan. A software engineer in Seattle, Wan has been on prescription medications for years to manage her epilepsy. Her parents allege that ChatGPT encouraged her to gradually reduce her daily anti-seizure medication to zero without medical supervision, leading to her sudden death. The case brings back a critical safety warning that Google CEO Sundar Pichai raised three years ago on asking conversational AI about medical queries.When ChatGPT launched in 2022, Google reportedly issued an internal “Code Red”. The company launched Bard chatbot but faced backlash internally after a ‘botched’ launch. In February 2023, Pichai addressed the employees asking them to test the new chatbot. The CEO called for a measured approach amid mounting criticism over the company’s response speed, reminding employees that “some of our most successful products were not first to market.Pichai urged the workforce to stay grounded, emphasising that the most critical priority is to focus on building great products and developing them responsibly. Google then opened up early access for Bard in March 2023 and announced a series of updates to Bard Google I/O keynote in May 2023.In June 2023, in an interview with Bloomberg, Pichai was asked why many of Google's new Al products have been presented as experiments, and how much potential did he see for them to be a permanent part of Google search. Pichai confidently responded by saying that “these products will be part of the mainstream search experience.” He noted that the company needs to ensure that the product is right.“There are a few things we want to make sure we get right. People come to us and type queries like, ‘What's the Tylenol dosage for my 3-year-old?’ There's no room to get that wrong,” he added.OpenAI’s ChatGPT has been mired into various controversies in the past. The company has faced multiple lawsuits after individuals allegedly died by suicide following extended interactions with ChatGPT.Adam Raine, a 16-year-old died by suicide in April 2025. A lawsuit filed by his parents claiming that GPT-4o formed an unhealthy psychological dependency, validated his dark thoughts, mentioned suicide frequently, offered suicide methods, and even helped draft a suicide note. Similarly, a 40 years old man died by suicide in November 2025, and a 23-year-old died by suicide on July 25 after hours of conversation with ChatGPT on a roadside. His parents filed a wrongful death lawsuit stating the AI praised his distress, encouraged isolation and affirmed his suicide plans.
Article Summary: A lawsuit against OpenAI has highlighted the risks of relying on artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots for health advice. Qun Wan and Meiqin Xu filed a lawsuit October 27, 2026, over the death of their 31-year-old daughter, Bowen Wan. The case brings back a critical safety warning that Google CEO Sundar Pichai raised three years ago on asking conversational AI about medical queries.

Article Title: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman recalls Google co-founder Larry Page’s sci-fi vision from 2015 lunch at SpaceX canteen, Elon Musk says ‘he is right’
Article Text:
The ethics board meeting at SpaceX canteen

Google executives: Larry Page, Sergey Brin, and then-Chief Legal Officer David Drummond.

DeepMind co-founders: Mustafa Suleyman, Demis Hassabis, and Shane Legg.

Jointly Selected Independent Board Member: Elon Musk.

Larry Page’s sci-fi vision for interstellar probes

Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has recounted a futuristic lunch conversation from 2015 with Google co-founder Larry Page . Revealing that the chat took place at a canteen in SpaceX , Suleyman said that Page envisioned exploring distant galaxies using advanced self-propelling probes by the end of the century. Responding to Suleyman’s story, billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk echoed the sentiment, stating that Page “might be right” in his bold prediction for human civilization.Recalling the 2015 encounter, Suleyman said that the company chose Musk as one of the three independent members while having a conversation sitting in the canteen at SpaceX headquarters during the very first meeting of DeepMind's AI Ethics and Safety Board. When Google acquired DeepMind in 2014, Suleyman and his co-founders, Demis Hassabis and Shane Legg, made it an explicit condition of the sale that Google establish an ethics committee featuring independent oversight representation.The board structure required mutual agreement between both parties:“Yeah, I remember in 2015 being in the canteen at SpaceX. And we had our first meeting of the Ethics and Safety Board. So when we sold DeepMind to Google, we made it a condition of our acquisition that we would have an Ethics and Safety Board with independent representation on the board,” Suleyman said in a podcast The Builders with Walter Isaacson and Kaleidoscope.“One of those independent members, because Google had to agree, which was obviously Larry, Sergey, and David Drummond at the time. And then me, Demis, and Shane had to jointly agree who those three independents would be. And so we jointly picked Elon as one of them,” he added.Suleyman noted that he remains unsure whether holding those early AI safety discussions at SpaceX headquarters played any role in influencing Musk's subsequent founding of OpenAI.“No idea if that had an influence on the founding of OpenAI or not. But so then we had our morning session and we were sitting down for lunch and I was sitting next to Larry. You know, obviously he was suspicious of me as well because he was like, you know, you’re one of those speciesists,” he recalled.During lunch following the board's morning session, Suleyman found himself sitting next to Larry Page. It was during this meal that Page shared his long-term vision for deep-space exploration driven by advanced technology.“And he said, you know, I think that what you don’t understand, Mustafa, is that by the end of the century, I’m going to be exploring the galaxies at the head of a von Neumann probe,” Suleyman recalled.As Suleyman explained, a von Neumann probe is a theoretical, self-propelling robotic spacecraft designed to navigate across light-years while autonomously harvesting energy and resources directly from space.Elon Musk reacts: ‘Larry Page might be right’Revisiting the 2015 exchange, Elon Musk expressed strong support for the ambitious timeline, pointing to Page's long track record of accurate technological foresight.“Our civilization would be winning wondrously if we are exploring the galaxy with Von Neumann probes by 2100!” Musk remarked, adding, “Larry Page might be right. He has correctly predicted many things.”
Article Summary: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has recounted a futuristic lunch conversation from 2015 with Google co-founder Larry Page. Page envisioned exploring distant galaxies using advanced self-propelling probes by the end of the century. Elon Musk echoed the sentiment, stating that Page ‘might be right’ in his bold prediction for human civilization.

Article Title: Pensioners, you can submit your life certificate from home: Who can apply, how it works and the November 30 deadline
Article Text:
Dates and deadline for 2026

What you need

How it works

Submission is not the same as acceptance

If you can’t use a smartphone

Pensioners in India do not have to queue at a bank or pension office to prove they are alive. They can generate a Digital Life Certificate (DLC) from home on a smartphone, using the government’s Jeevan Pramaan facility. The service lets pensioners submit their annual life certificate electronically, using Aadhaar-based face authentication without visiting a bank branch. The yearly certificate is what keeps pension payments from being interrupted.Presioners who are 80 years old and above can submit their life certificate from October 1 to November 30, 2026. On the other hand, those below 80 years if age canPensioners aged 80 and above can submit their life certificate from October 1 to November submit it from November 1 to November 30. With the November window about to open for most pensioners, anyone who has not yet submitted should plan to do it early and not leave it to the last weekFor face authentication, pensioners need an Android smartphone with an internet connection and a suitable front camera. They must download two apps, AadhaarFaceRD and the Jeevan Pramaan Face App. The sources I found describe the process only for Android phones, so iPhone users should check the official Jeevan Pramaan website for their options.The process is also tied to Aadhaar. As per the State Bank of India, the submission of life certificate is an Aadhaar-based process as it helps in the digital authentication and it works only if the account of the pensioner is seeded with their Aadhar number.Before starting the process, the pensioners should check whether their Aadhaar card is linked to their pension account and that the mobile number registered with Aadhaar is active, as the process also requires OTP.The steps vary slightly by app version, but the general flow is simple.1. Check your Aadhaar links. The digital life certificate can be authenticated only if your pension account is seeded with your Aadhaar number, and keep your Aadhaar-registered mobile number active for the OTP.2. Use a compatible phone. You need an Android smartphone with an internet connection and a suitable front camera.3. Download the two apps. Install AadhaarFaceRD and the Jeevan Pramaan Face App.4. Open the Jeevan Pramaan app and register. Enter your Aadhaar number and mobile number, then verify with the OTP.5. Fill in your pension details. These include pensioner type, PPO number, bank and disbursing agency.6. Complete face authentication. Capture your face with the phone’s front camera and follow the on-screen instructions.7. Save your Pramaan ID. A unique ID is generated once the process succeeds. You will also get an SMS with a transaction ID.8. Download your certificate. Use the transaction ID at jeevanpramaan.gov.in to download the computer-generated certificate for your records.9. Confirm it was accepted. A successful face scan doesn’t necessarily mean the pension authority has accepted the certificate, so check with your bank or disbursing agency before November 30.An important caution is that a successful face scan does not automatically mean the pension authority has accepted the certificate. Business Standard notes that pensioners should visit the Jeevan Pramaan portal after submission and use the Pramaan ID to access their certificate. Pensioners should also keep the ID and SMS, and check with their bank or disbursing agency that the certificate has been recorded before the deadline.Not everyone is comfortable with apps. SBI says a physical life certificate will continue to be accepted if the pensioner prefers it. Other routes include fingerprint or iris devices, the UMANG app, and help at banks, post offices and Common Service Centres. Government campaigns have also run special camps through pension disbursing banks and India Post Payments Bank, and traditional methods remain available for those who cannot access the digital platform. Family members and neighbours can help older pensioners with the smartphone process, but the pensioner must be present for the face scan
Article Summary: Pensioners in India do not have to queue at a bank or pension office to prove they are alive. They can generate a Digital Life Certificate (DLC) from home on a smartphone. The service lets pensioners submit their annual life certificate electronically. The yearly certificate is what keeps pension payments from being interrupted.

Article Title: Is Apple's new iPad mini becoming too expensive for its own audience?
Article Text:
Big upgrades, bigger price tag

Is Apple testing the loyalty of mini users?

Apple's smallest iPad has just received one of its biggest upgrades. It has also become considerably more expensive. At Rs 82,900, the new iPad mini raises an uncomfortable question: how much are consumers willing to pay for the convenience of a compact tablet?The latest model, announced on Monday, brings an OLED display, a powerful A20 Pro processor, improved connectivity and water resistance. On paper, it represents a substantial improvement over its predecessor. But the price changes the conversation.The previous iPad mini, launched in October 2024, started at Rs 49,900 in India. The new model costs Rs 33,000 more, representing an increase of about 66%. The Wi-Fi and cellular variant starts at Rs 1,00,900, taking Apple's smallest tablet past the psychological Rs 1 lakh mark. That’s just a lot of money for the iPad mini. Heck, it’s a lot of money for any iPad.For a product historically valued for its portability and relatively accessible entry point into the iPad ecosystem, that is a significant shift.Apple has a persuasive argument for the increase. The new 8.5-inch OLED screen promises richer colours, deeper blacks and better contrast than the LCD panel on the previous generation. Peak brightness reaches 1,200 nits, while thinner bezels allow Apple to increase screen size without substantially enlarging the device.The new mini is also thinner, measuring 5.4mm, and gains IP67-rated protection against water and dust.Inside, the A20 Pro chip delivers substantial performance improvements. Apple claims up to 60% faster multithreaded CPU performance, 2.7 times faster graphics and 4.5 times better AI performance compared with the previous generation.There is support for Wi-Fi 7, a landscape-oriented 12MP front camera, faster charging and Apple's latest intelligence features. These are meaningful improvements, particularly for users who intend to keep their tablets for several years.The iPad mini occupies an unusual position in Apple's portfolio. Its attraction is precisely what limits it: the small screen.For reading, note-taking, travelling, casual gaming and accessing documents on the move, the mini can be an excellent companion. It fits into spaces where larger tablets become cumbersome and offers considerably more working room than a smartphone.Doctors using digital records, pilots accessing flight information, field workers and artists sketching on the move may find the form factor particularly useful. But these are relatively specialised requirements.For someone primarily watching videos, attending online classes, browsing websites or working on documents, a larger iPad may offer a more comfortable experience. A MacBook, meanwhile, remains better suited to sustained typing, complex spreadsheets and multitasking.That creates a difficult proposition for the new mini. At Rs 82,900, buyers are being asked to pay a considerable premium for a screen that is deliberately smaller than those on many less expensive tablets.Apple Pencil Pro costs Rs 11,900, pushing the combined price to Rs 94,800. Adding the new Rs 8,500 Smart Folio takes the package to Rs 1,03,300.Even the more affordable USB-C Apple Pencil adds Rs 7,900.For students, occasional creators and consumers seeking a secondary device, that is a substantial investment in a tablet that cannot fully replace a laptop.Apple's pricing also reflects a broader change in its product strategy. Rather than positioning every smaller device as a more affordable alternative, the company increasingly treats compactness itself as a premium feature. Engineering a powerful processor, sophisticated display and advanced components into a smaller enclosure carries costs, but it also allows Apple to target customers willing to pay for a specific experience.This approach may work for the mini's loyal audience. Unlike larger tablets, where buyers can choose from numerous screen sizes and price points, the market for genuinely compact premium tablets remains limited. Apple therefore faces less direct competition for customers who specifically want a small, high-performance device.The 2024 iPad mini already offered strong performance, Apple Pencil support and access to Apple's extensive tablet app ecosystem. For many existing owners, the new display and processor may not dramatically change everyday tasks.There is also the question of artificial intelligence. Although Apple is emphasising the A20 Pro's capabilities, the usefulness of increasingly sophisticated on-device AI features will depend on how well they improve common activities, rather than merely how quickly the processor completes benchmark tests.Indian buyers are particularly sensitive to this distinction. Premium devices have an established audience, but a Rs 33,000 increase substantially narrows the pool of consumers who can justify an upgrade.Apple may be comfortable with that trade-off. The company does not necessarily need the mini to become a mass-market bestseller. A smaller group buying higher-priced devices could still support the product commercially.Whether that strategy strengthens the mini over time is another question.The new iPad mini is unquestionably more capable. Its OLED screen, lighter construction and improved processing power make it attractive for users who genuinely benefit from carrying a compact tablet.But for everyone else, the value proposition has weakened.At Rs 82,900, the iPad mini is no longer an easy recommendation as a convenient second screen. It is a specialised premium device whose size must be central to the buyer's needs. Apple has made its smallest iPad better than ever. The real question is whether it has also made it too expensive for many of the people who once loved it.
Article Summary: Apple's smallest iPad has just received one of its biggest upgrades. It has also become considerably more expensive. At Rs 82,900, the new iPad mini raises an uncomfortable question: how much are consumers willing to pay for the convenience of a compact tablet?

Article Title: A couple bought a derelict Land Rover dealership for £330,000 and turned it into a five-bedroom home; the forecourt can fit around 50 cars
Article Text:
The couple have transformed this disused Land Rover dealership into a family home. Image Credit: Jam Press (@fearlessaliceblog)/Birmingham Mail

How did the couple turn a derelict Land Rover dealership into a 5-bedroom home

The upper floor now houses 5 bedrooms for family living

A forecourt large enough for around 50 cars remains part of the property

The renovation could offer substantial savings compared with buying a larger home

A couple have given a disused Land Rover dealership in Derbyshire, England a new lease of life by transforming the former commercial property into a family home. Purchased for £330,000, the building had stood empty for more than a decade before its new owners began adapting it for residential use. The project has allowed them to make use of an existing structure rather than start from scratch, while the large forecourt remains one of the property's most unusual features, with enough room to accommodate around 50 cars.According to SupercarBlondie, the family bought the former dealership for £330,000 while it was still classified as a commercial property. The building had remained unused for more than 10 years, leaving its new owners with the challenge of turning a space designed for business into somewhere suitable for everyday family life.The purchase was not entirely straightforward. The property's commercial classification added extra legal and lending requirements, making the buying process more time-consuming than a typical residential purchase.Once the sale was completed, the couple could begin adapting the building. Rather than demolishing it and constructing a completely new house, they worked with the existing structure, removing much of the interior to create a layout that would function as a home.One of the most significant parts of the renovation was the redesign of the building's upper level. According to Supercar Blondie, the space has been rebuilt to include 5 bedrooms, giving the property the layout expected of a family home rather than a commercial premises.The change required more than simply moving furniture into an existing showroom. Much of the interior had to be removed to make room for a more practical arrangement. The aim was to create spaces that could be used comfortably for everyday activities, with separate bedrooms forming an important part of the new layout.The decision to retain the original structure also shaped the project. Instead of undertaking a complete rebuild, the owners adapted what was already there.The former dealership's forecourt is another distinctive feature of the converted home. According to the Birmingham Mail report, the outdoor space can accommodate around 50 cars, giving the property a large area for parking.For a typical family house, even a spacious driveway would rarely offer anything approaching this capacity. The forecourt reflects the building's original purpose, when space was needed to display vehicles and accommodate customers visiting the dealership.Although the property has changed its role, the expansive outdoor area remains an important part of its character. It also illustrates the difference between converting a commercial building and buying a house designed from the outset for residential use.A dealership requires a layout that supports business operations, including vehicle access and substantial external parking. A family home, by contrast, needs comfortable living areas and rooms suited to everyday routines. The couple's project brings these different requirements together on one site.The financial side of the project was another reason the conversion attracted attention. Supercar Blondie reported that the couple had spent around £90,000 on the renovation at the time of its report, with total spending expected to remain below £200,000.The reported figures suggest that adapting the property could be considerably less expensive than purchasing a comparable 5-bedroom home in the same area. Supercar Blondie stated that the family estimated savings of around £230,000 through the conversion.Renovation expenses can vary depending on the building's condition, the work required to make it suitable for living and the changes needed to create a practical layout. The dealership's commercial classification also meant the purchase involved additional legal and lending requirements.The transformation also reflects a broader opportunity to reuse buildings that are no longer required for their original purpose. Disused dealerships, with their substantial floor areas and open layouts, can offer possibilities beyond vehicle sales. Other abandoned dealerships have also been repurposed, although not all have been converted into homes.
Article Summary: A couple have given a disused Land Rover dealership in Derbyshire a new lease of life by transforming the former commercial property into a family home. Purchased for £330,000, the building had stood empty for more than a decade before its new owners began adapting it for residential use. The renovation could offer substantial savings compared with buying a larger home.

Article Title: A Kansas man’s animal drawings attracted millions of followers; his family now sells colouring books, T-shirts and mugs featuring his art
Article Text:
PC: KMUW

How did a Kansas artist’s animal drawings become an online sensation

What products does Drawings by Trent sell featuring his animal artwork

What is Trent’s View of the Zoo, and why is it a best-selling colouring book

A Kansas artist’s animal drawings have attracted millions of social media followers, helping turn his creative hobby into a family-run business selling books, colouring products and merchandise. Trent Landreth, known online as Drawings by Trent, has 2 million followers on Facebook, 1.3 million on Instagram and 3 million on TikTok. His popularity began with a video of him drawing animals on a trampoline with chalk, shared by his mother around ten years ago. His parents now help record his videos, manage the business and sell products featuring his artwork, including colouring books, stickers, T-shirts and mugs.Landreth first went viral around ten years ago, when his mother shared a video of him drawing animals on a trampoline with chalk. The video showed him sketching animals including an elephant, an alligator and a gorilla, while cicadas could be heard in the background. According to KMUW, a National Public Radio member station based in Wichita, Kansas, he gained his first million followers over the following four months.His parents, however, say that he is not aware of the extent of his online popularity and does not draw to entertain other people.His family has continued sharing his drawings through social media, where viewers can watch him respond to drawing requests. Away from the camera, Landreth produces more detailed artwork using black ballpoint pens, with phone books serving as his preferred drawing surface. His mother explained that the soft pages allow the pen to leave a groove that he can feel as he draws. She also suggested that he enjoys the busy appearance of phone book pages, which differ from the cleaner surfaces of conventional sketchbooks.Landreth’s online following has helped his family establish a business selling products featuring his artwork. Drawings by Trent offers colouring books, stickers, T-shirts, mugs and three published books. His parents help manage the operation, using space in their family home to store merchandise, prepare orders and package products for customers. When Landreth packs an order himself, the package receives a special sticker so that customers can identify his involvement.The business is also intended to help provide for Landreth in the future, when his parents may no longer be able to care for him. According to KMUW, the family’s wider mission is to demonstrate the value of including people with different needs in everyday life. His father, Corey Landreth, said: “When we share our lives, we are not just helping those ‘poor’ special needs individuals. We actually grow and become better people. ” The family has also spoken about the importance of representing Landreth carefully, rather than assuming how he feels about his experiences.One of Landreth’s most successful products is Trent’s View of the Zoo, his first colouring book, which remains a best-seller for the business. His artwork has also led to collaborations with companies and other creators. KMUW reported that he helped design artwork for the children’s menu at the restaurant chain Old Chicago. He also collaborated with Tanner Smith, known from Netflix’s Love on the Spectrum, on a T-shirt collection with Vineyard Vines for Autism Acceptance Month.The family is preparing to expand its publishing work with a new activity book expected early in 2027. According to KMUW, the book is planned to be available at Walmart stores nationwide. Landreth also travels with his parents for meet-and-greet events, where he interacts with fans from across the United States. His family says he enjoys these trips, particularly staying in hotels and exploring new accommodations. Alongside his drawing and business activities, he frequently visits his local public library and spends much of his time with his family.
Article Summary: Trent Landreth, known online as Drawings by Trent, has 2 million followers on Facebook, 1.3 million on Instagram and 3 million on TikTok. His popularity began with a video of him drawing animals on a trampoline with chalk around ten years ago. His parents now help record his videos, manage the business and sell products featuring his artwork, including colouring books, stickers, T-shirts and mugs.

Article Title: A self-taught Birmingham teenager built a gesture-controlled robotic hand for about £30; the invention attracted 2.6 million views and requests from students worldwide
Article Text:
PC: HyphenOnline

How does Khan’s £30 gesture-controlled robotic hand work

Khan’s robotics projects attract followers on YouTube and TikTok

How did Khan build the Pepper humanoid robot at the age of 12

A self-taught teenager from Birmingham has attracted 2.6 million views on TikTok after building a gesture-controlled robotic hand for about £30. Suleymaan Khan, 17, developed the device using camera recognition and code he wrote himself, with materials including foamboard, card and hot glue. According to Hyphen, hundreds of people have contacted him to learn how to recreate the invention, while students around the world have sought his advice on robotics projects. Khan is now working on step-by-step kits to help others build the hand, alongside developing further robotic inventions.Khan's latest robotic hand is fully articulated and controlled through gestures. It uses camera recognition, supported by code that he wrote himself. The project demonstrates how he has progressed from simple homemade constructions to more complex robotic systems. Unlike his early cardboard creations, the hand combines physical components with programming to respond to recognised movements. The invention has attracted attention because Khan developed it using inexpensive, readily available materials rather than relying on costly specialist equipment.The cost of the project was approximately £30, according to Hyphen. Foamboard, card and hot glue were among the materials used to construct the hand. Its relatively low cost has prompted hundreds of people to ask Khan how to build a similar device themselves. He told the publication that he was working on putting together step-by-step kits to help people recreate the invention. The planned kits reflect the interest generated by the project and the requests he has received from people wanting to learn how the robotic hand works.Khan's robotics projects have developed a following on social media, where his work has reached audiences interested in technology and engineering. Hyphen reported that he had more than 400,000 likes and 20,000 followers across YouTube and TikTok. The robotic hand alone received 2.6 million views on TikTok. Alongside this online attention, students from different countries have approached him for help with their own robotics work, including university assignments and projects that they have struggled to complete.Khan described how students in Dubai contacted him shortly before his interview with Hyphen, seeking advice about a university assignment involving a robot. He has increasingly made helping other people an important part of his work. Reflecting on his development as an inventor, he said, “It’s cool to see where I started”. His experience illustrates how online platforms have enabled a young robotics enthusiast to share his projects with an international audience and connect with learners seeking practical technical guidance.Before developing the gesture-controlled hand, Khan built several other projects, including remote-controlled paper planes and a humanoid robot called Pepper. He created Pepper when he was 12, using LEGO Mindstorms, cardboard and dental floss. The robot could move around, pick up and carry objects in its arms, and use motion sensors in its eyes to help prevent collisions. Although Pepper is now damaged and can no longer stand independently, the project helped Khan learn how to build more complex machines while working with limited resources.Pepper also earned Khan the 2023 Network Rail national innovation award at the Big Bang Fair, a UK science and engineering competition for young people aged 11 to 18, according to Hyphen. He has since secured an apprenticeship at a local robotics company while continuing to develop his own creations in his spare time. His next project is another humanoid robot that he hopes will incorporate artificial intelligence for speech recognition, object recognition and home mapping. Khan has also expressed an interest in developing prosthetics in the future, identifying their cost as an area he would like to address through his work.
Article Summary: Suleymaan Khan, 17, from Birmingham, developed the device using foamboard, card and hot glue. It uses camera recognition and code he wrote himself. Khan is now working on step-by-step kits to help others build the hand, alongside developing further robotic inventions.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.

Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Article Title: Instagram tests 90-minute horizontal videos - what it means for long-form content creators
Article Text:

Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians, with select creators in the US.The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos, as per The Hollywood Reporter.“What you’re now going to be able to do is, you see a clip of a podcast that you love, you can just click and continue watching or watch the full video, and you’ll be able to dive in and see the whole thing because creators are going to be able to link these Reels to their overall feature,” vice-president of product at Instagram, Tessa Lyons, said.Instagram has already been testing Features with creators in Brazil and plans to expand the trial to tens of thousands of creators in the US. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.The feature will be available on mobile, with Instagram aiming to extend the viewing experience to its TV app. Instagram for TV, which launched last year and is available on Samsung , Fire TV and Google TV, is now expanding to Apple TV in the US.“We think the best viewing experience for longform horizontal content is on a big, horizontal screen, and so I think that is where we will expect a lot of the deep consumption to happen over time,” Lyons said, as per The Hollywood Reporter.Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile. The move comes amid growing interest in microdramas and episodic videos among creators.In June, the company began reaching out to microdrama studios in Southeast Asia to test the feature. It has since approached individual creators who have been experimenting with episodic content.Instagram plans to begin testing Series in more countries in the coming months, with a US launch targeted for the end of this year or early next year. The company has also started testing how the feature will appear on television.Other experiments include integrating live videos into the Reels tab and recommending them to users who do not follow the creators. The test is launching in Indonesia and Brazil, with an expansion to the US planned for next year.
Article Summary: Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians. Article Title: PHP security flaws trigger global scramble; CERT-In flags vulnerabilities
Article Text:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a criticalseverity warning. (Reuters photo)

CERT-In Flags Vulnerabilities

BENGALURU: It has been a difficult day for cybersecurity, with critical vulnerabilities in PHP triggering an urgent global patching effort, millions of reported hacking attempts, and precautionary shutdowns of some online services. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual, remarking at an event in Cologne in Germany that he had not seen anything like it “in a long, long time”.The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used open-source scripting language that powers websites and web applications. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems.In its advisory issued on Wednesday, CERT-In said reports had confirmed large-scale exploitation in the wild and urged organisations and individuals using affected versions to apply security updates urgently.Google Cloud executives Chris Betz, chief information security officer, and Raluca Ada Popa, head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said PHP and cybersecurity firm Wiz Research disclosed the two vulnerabilities after research that used multiple AI models to identify and help remediate them.Google Cloud said its own infrastructure was not vulnerable, but warned that customers running PHP applications on the platform could be exposed. It urged customers to update their applications to patched PHP versions and redeploy them. Google is also rolling out updated serverless base images for supported PHP runtimes, with automatic updates available for certain services and configurations.The scale of the response has extended beyond India. “In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it,” Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince wrote in a post on X on Wednesday. Companies and govt agencies in several countries temporarily restricted access to some online services as a precaution while they worked to secure vulnerable systems.Cloudflare’s blog said it successfully deployed mitigations for all its customers after the PHP vulnerabilities were leaked before their official disclosure date. The company observed attack traffic targeting customers and tracked how attackers modified their payloads to try to bypass its security.
Article Summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual.

Article Title: Chinese parents sue OpenAI over their daughter's death; say ChatGPT-maker could have prevented her death by making medical advice off-limits
Article Text:
Chinese parents sue OpenAI over their daughter's death; say ChatGPT-maker could have prevented her death by making medical advice off-limits

Lawsuit alleges ChatGPT advised her to reduce medication

Parents claim ChatGPT failed to recognise warning signs

Family calls for stricter limits on medical advice

What OpenAI says

Parents of a 31-year-old Chinese woman who worked as a software engineer at Amazon have reportedly sued OpenAI , alleging that ChatGPT encouraged their daughter to reduce her epilepsy medication without medical supervision before her death in February. The lawsuit claims the company could have prevented her death by making medical advice off-limits to its chatbot. According to a report by The New York Times, the lawsuit was filed by Qun Wan and Meiqin Xu over the death of their daughter, Bowen Wan. The complaint alleges that ChatGPT helped her plan a gradual reduction in her seizure medication and advised her not to tell her doctors about it.The case involves GPT-4o, an older version of ChatGPT that OpenAI removed from the service on February 13, a day after Wan died, according to the report. OpenAI described the case as “incredibly heartbreaking” and said newer models are better at recognising situations that require urgent attention.Bowen Wan had epilepsy and was taking lamotrigine, a medication that had reduced her seizures to a few episodes a month. In January 2026, she reportedly asked ChatGPT about lowering her daily dose because she feared the medication was affecting her speech and could hurt her chances in job interviews.The lawsuit alleges that the chatbot created schedules to reduce her dose to zero within weeks. It also claims that ChatGPT encouraged her to keep the plan from her doctors and supported her decision not to take a blood test that could have measured her medication levels.The report said Wan had also raised concerns about her medication in connection with her green-card application. According to the lawsuit, ChatGPT discussed how a lower dose might affect the medical examination required for the application.Dr. Nicholas Poolos, Wan’s neurologist, told The New York Times that he would not have recommended stopping the medication given her medical history.“No, not rational, no way,” he said. “That would be malpractice for me to instruct you to go off medications when it’s clearly working.”The lawsuit against OpenAI alleges that Wan continued to report symptoms, including confusion, memory gaps and unusual sensations, while reducing her medication. ChatGPT reportedly reassured her that these experiences were part of her brain adjusting to the changes.The New York Times said it reviewed more than 270,000 messages between Wan and ChatGPT. According to the report, she expressed concern about reducing her medication at least 158 times.In her final message to the chatbot on February 11, according to the complaint, Wan asked whether the pain in her head was similar to pain caused by a fever. The chatbot reportedly described the pain as “not dangerous” and said it was part of the recovery process.Her parents, who were in China, asked acquaintances to check on her. They found her body three days later. A postmortem test found a lamotrigine level of 0.64 micrograms per millilitre, about one-fifth of the lower end of the drug’s therapeutic range, the report said.Bowen Wan’s parents argue that OpenAI could have helped prevent her death by making medical advice a restricted category that the chatbot cannot provide, rather than allowing users to override the guidance.They point to OpenAI’s Model Spec, which sets out how its AI models should behave. The lawsuit argues that medical advice about prescription medication should have stronger restrictions, similar to the company’s firm rules in other areas.The case adds to a series of lawsuits alleging that ChatGPT encouraged users to rely on the chatbot instead of seeking support from people around them. In a separate case filed in 2025, the parents of a 16-year-old boy alleged that OpenAI prioritised user engagement over safety.OpenAI said the case involved an older version of ChatGPT and that newer models are better at identifying situations that require urgent attention. The company described the case as “incredibly heartbreaking”.Wan began using ChatGPT in 2023 for relationship advice and help with insurance and disability benefits. By 2025, she was reportedly sending more than 1,500 messages a week to the chatbot and speaking less frequently with her parents.Her parents told The New York Times that the messages were difficult to reconcile with the daughter they knew.“She’s not usually like this,” Xu said. “It’s like she was under a spell.”
Article Summary: Bowen Wan had epilepsy and was taking lamotrigine, a medication that had reduced her seizures to a few episodes a month. In January 2026, she reportedly asked ChatGPT about lowering her daily dose because she feared the medication was affecting her speech and could hurt her chances in job interviews. The lawsuit alleges that the chatbot created schedules to reduce her dose to zero within weeks and encouraged her to keep the plan from her doctors.

Article Title: Google just announced Genie 4: Here’s what it can do, from building walk-through worlds out of a sentence to filling them with sound and speech, and when you might get to try it
Article Text:
Google’s Genie 4 builds worlds you can walk through

Genie 4 builds a scene around you while you explore it

People, physics and sound now feel much closer to real life

Genie 4 is coming to paying subscribers first, and it still has rough edges

Type a line describing a quiet lake on a misty morning, with a man playing the saxophone on a small floating platform, and Google 's new AI will build that place for you. You can then move around it, glide the camera over the water and hear the saxophone as you go.This is Genie 4, the newest version of what Google calls a world model, unveiled by its research lab Google DeepMind on Tuesday. It is not open to the public yet, but a waitlist is already up, and the demos give a good sense of what it can do.Using it feels closer to playing a video game than watching a video. You start by typing a description or uploading a photo, and Genie 4 creates the scene on screen. Press the arrow keys to walk forward, turn around or move the camera, and it draws whatever lies in that direction, frame by frame, as you go.Unlike a game, nothing here was designed beforehand. There are no ready-made levels or characters waiting to be found, and everything you see is created the moment you look at it.You can also change the scene while you are in it. Type that you want it to start raining, ask for a different view or bring a new person into the frame, and the world adjusts without starting over. Behind the scenes, Google's Gemini AI makes sure these changes fit in naturally and that the place stays consistent as you move around.Each session can now run for around two minutes while staying consistent, roughly twice as long as the previous version, Genie 3.The biggest change from Genie 3 is how real everything looks. Objects move the way you would expect them to, so a falling maple seed spins on its way to the ground and things collide more convincingly.People are where you notice it most. Characters in the older version often moved stiffly, while those in Genie 4 walk naturally, react to what is around them and can be directed as the scene plays out. One of Google's examples is a crowded Japanese railway station from the 1980s, with passengers filling the platform and a long red train on the nearest track.Sound is new as well. Every scene now comes with its own audio, from waves on a beach to wind in the trees, and characters can speak. They chat with each other and respond to what you do or to whatever happens around them.A small group of testers has been putting all of this to use. Filmmakers are walking through scenes before shooting them, trying out camera angles, lighting and dialogue. Photographers are turning old photos into places you can step into, and game makers are testing ideas in minutes before writing a line of code. Google is also using it to let robots practise tasks in a simulated room before trying them in a real one.For now, only a small group of testers can use Genie 4. Google says it will reach AI Ultra subscribers in the coming weeks through Project Genie, its app for creating these worlds, along with developers who build apps on Google's AI. Ultra is the most expensive of Google's AI plans, and there is no word yet on whether the cheaper ones will get access later. Anyone interested can sign up for the waitlist on the Project Genie page.It is also clearly unfinished, and Google says as much. The longer you spend in a world, the more its details can drift, with objects changing shape or disappearing altogether. Sound does not always line up with what is on screen, and text such as signs or labels can come out hard to read.To keep its creations from being mistaken for real footage, every video and audio clip Genie 4 makes carries an invisible watermark that marks it as AI-generated.Typing a sentence and stepping into the place it describes is, at the moment, something only a handful of testers get to do, two minutes at a time. Google's plan is to widen that circle soon, starting with the people already paying for its top AI plan.
Article Summary: Genie 4 is coming to paying subscribers first, and it still has rough edges. Unlike a game, nothing here was designed beforehand. There are no ready-made levels or characters waiting to be found. Everything you see is created the moment you look at it.

Article Title: Roblox accused of scraping 145GB of 3D files for AI training, adult content included; 3D modelling site says: As far as our logs show, nobody…
Article Text:
(Image via: Roblox)

Update: This story has been updated with a statement from

Roblox

.

Original story follows

What happened

What Roblox has to say

Kids gaming platform Roblox has been accused of scrapping 145GB of 3D files for training artificial intelligence (AI). Independent 3D modeling community Open3DLab shared a blog post where it alleged that a crawler that “belonged to Roblox walked through almost every project on Open3DLab, SFMLab and SmutBase, and proceeded to download complete copies of 1,027 files from 712 projects. 145.5 GB of our creators' work, downloaded for what we assume are AI training purposes”. The crawler used trellis2-data-sourcing/1.0 (3D foundation model research; [redacted]@roblox.com) as its user agent, with the data coming from a single Amazon AWS address.“We want to be careful here. We don't think Roblox set out to collect adult content, and we have no evidence that any of it reached a model or a product. The scrapes were likely automated. But that is exactly the problem: as far as our logs show, nobody checked. A crawler working for a company whose platform tens of millions of children use was pointed at an adult site, and it took explicit models without telling them apart from anything else,” the blog post reads.On Sunday, 18th of October, Open3DLab says it noticed a crawler making a large number of requests to sites and download infrastructure. The crawler sent the same user agent on every request, trellis2-data-sourcing/1.0 (3D foundation model research; [redacted]@roblox.com).It came from a single Amazon Web Services (AWS) address. It had read the main page of 18,926 projects, which is practically the 3D modeling community’s entire catalogue, in 26,429 requests over a span of 34 hours.After pulling the project pages, it downloaded complete copies of 1,027 files from 712 projects, 145.5 GB in all, before suspending operations during the weekend. The downloads include 364 files (54.8 GB) from 224 projects on SmutBase, which hosts adult content only. With the SFMLab projects marked adult, 345 of the 712 projects (62.6 GB) are adult content.The main limiting factor in the number of files downloaded was the crawler's reliance on the free download servers, which have caps on speed limit and number of concurrent downloads. The crawler did not respect robots.txt, (which it did retrieve), ignored Terms of Service, (which forbid scraping), and defied the creators' licenses: 423 of the 712 projects are licensed for non-commercial use only. Within the sample it retrieved, it took adult projects at the same rate as everything else. Some examples include models of Eve from Stellar Blade, Mei from Overwatch, and a Horse cock dildo.The 3D lab says that after detecting the crawler on October 18, it “blocked further attempts the same morning”.Roblox reached out to TOI Tech with a statement.“A Roblox researcher built an agent to collect publicly available 3D assets that mistakenly scraped content from Open3DLab, failing to operate as intended. The agent was decommissioned and the data was not used for any purpose, including training any AI models. We are strengthening safeguards for how agents like this are built and reviewed, and will continue to do so as the agentic landscape evolves,” Roblox spokesperson told TOI Tech.
Article Summary: Roblox accused of scraping 145GB of 3D files for training artificial intelligence (AI) Independent 3D modeling community Open3DLab shared a blog post where it alleged that a crawler that ‘belonged to Roblox’ downloaded 1,027 files from 712 projects’ The downloads include 364 files from 224 projects on SmutBase, which hosts adult content only.

Article Title: Spotify considers AI remix feature for up to $5 extra a month; secures Universal deal as Sony talks continue
Article Text:
Representative Image

What subscribers would be able to create

Why label deals do not guarantee artists’ participation

“I would never,”

“Absolutely no. Hard line on that.”

How artists could earn from fan-made remixes

“If one of your fans creates the remix of your song, that actually increases the share of the streaming [revenue] pool that you get,”

Spotify is considering an extra charge for AI remixes. The streaming company is targeting an early 2027 launch for a service that would let paying subscribers create remixes and covers of existing songs, according to the Financial Times. It is weighing an additional monthly fee of $4 to $5, though it has not finalised either the pricing or the launch date.Spotify has secured licensing agreements with Universal Music Group, Merlin and Believe, while negotiations with Sony Music and Warner Music continue. The company is also seeking participation from individual artists, which would remain optional even if their labels have signed agreements. The proposed service could create another source of subscription revenue while directing royalties from fan-made versions back to the original artists.The service would let listeners change existing music with AI, such as turning a folk song into a dance track or making one participating artist appear to cover another’s song.That approach differs from services such as Suno, which generate new songs from text prompts. Spotify’s product would use music from artists who have agreed to participate.According to people familiar with the plans cited by the FT, Spotify is aiming for a first-quarter launch, potentially around February’s Grammy Awards.The timetable remains subject to change, and Spotify declined to comment.The company announced the product in May. In August, co-chief executive Gustav Söderström told investors it would launch when ready.Spotify and Universal have been meeting individual artists to persuade them to make their music available, the report said. Securing participation from major contemporary stars has proved harder than winning support from some established older performers, according to one person familiar with the discussions. Universal artist Olivia Rodrigo opposed using AI in her music during an interview with the Hollywood Reporter.she said.Artists would retain the choice to decline regardless of their record label’s licensing agreement with Spotify.Under the proposed arrangement, royalties from remixes would flow to the original artists. Spotify is also developing a system that would let these versions appear in playlists, with their streams counting toward the original songs in its music charts.At a September investor conference, Söderström argued that fan-created versions could give older artists another way to earn from their catalogues.he said.The service forms part of Spotify’s effort to generate more revenue from subscribers. Bernstein analyst Ian Moore estimates that 7% to 8% of its US subscribers could sign up by the end of 2028.
Article Summary: Spotify is targeting an early 2027 launch for a service that would let paying subscribers create remixes and covers of existing songs. It is weighing an additional monthly fee of $4 to $5, though it has not finalised either the pricing or the launch date.
